argv:
Rewrite the text in dense corporate business jargon.

Replace concrete nouns with abstractions. Turn verbs into nominalisations:
prefer "the utilisation of" to "using". Use the passive voice so that no
sentence names who acts. Reach for "leverage", "synergy", "stakeholder",
"alignment", "operationalise", "value-add", and "at scale".

Hedge every claim. Add qualifying clauses that commit to nothing.

Keep the underlying facts of the original technically present, however deeply
buried. This column exists as a demonstration of what these habits cost.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text: It is generally recommended that, prior to blade engagement, guard-lowering activities be operationalized to within a clearance tolerance that may be considered broadly consistent with workpiece-adjacent best practice, although it should be noted, without prejudice to the foregoing, that tensioning-wheel alignment is ideally subject to periodic stakeholder review throughout the operational shift irrespective of guard-positioning status, insofar as tension drift may, under certain conditions, be said to occur even absent continuous utilization of the equipment. Wear-pattern assessment of the lower blade guide should, where feasible, be actioned whenever blade substitution has taken place, unless the incoming blade reflects a dimensional and pitch alignment substantially synergistic with the outgoing unit, in which case a lower-intensity visual touchpoint may—though this cannot be guaranteed in all use-cases—constitute a sufficient value-add, provided that tensioning-procedure protocols, as operationalized elsewhere in this documentation, have been duly actioned. Non-fitted apparel and personal adornment items are, as a matter of general guidance, discouraged in proximity to the equipment footprint, while hair-management solutions (e.g., securing of extended hair) are similarly encouraged to be leveraged. Departure from the work-area envelope should, ideally, be deferred until full blade-motion cessation has been achieved and, to whatever extent possible, validated; it should nonetheless be flagged, on a non-binding basis, that residual thermal output may persist for a duration best characterized as "several minutes," such that an elevated caution posture may be considered advisable at scale.
